title: Pricing SKU consolidation: launch cadence, release notes, and GTM readiness
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Summary: Consolidate existing SKU surface into a simplified tiered SKU model and coordinate cross-team launch work: release notes, billing migration, sales enablement, and customer communications. Goal is to reduce customer confusion, improve metering accuracy, and unlock clearer upsell paths while preserving revenue neutrality for existing customers over the 6-month grandfathering window.

Scope:
- Replace legacy per-feature SKUs (storage, active-concurrency, dedicated-throughput) with three primary SKUs: Core, Dedicated, and Private Add-on.
- Introduce per-route limits and default quotas that map to existing customers with automatic migration rules.
- Update billing pipeline for new SKU ids and audit logs; ensure correct usage attribution in invoices.
- Coordinate release notes across Console, API docs, SDK changelogs, and Billing Help Center articles.

Business trade-offs considered:
- Revenue neutrality vs. simplicity: decided on 6-month grandfathering + opt-in pricing experiments for high-volume customers to avoid immediate revenue disruption.
- Strict vs. permissive migration: chosen permissive migration with telemetry checks and merchant opt-out within first 30 days.
- Timing: prefer staggered regional rollout (NA -> EU -> APAC) to reduce blast radius and allow legal/compliance regional checks.

Key stakeholders: PM (Sofia Ramirez), ENG owners (Liam Zhang - billing infra), Runtime (Priya Patel), Console (Jorge Alvarez), Sales Enablement (Maya O'Neill), Legal/Finance (Hannah Lee), Support (Marcus Boone).

Artifacts & links (single source of truth):
- Confluence: pricing-repackaging/sku-mapping (detailed SKU table + migration mapping)
- Drive: Sales_SKU_Migration_v2 deck (shared with GTM)
- GitHub: redwood/billing PRs: #4123 (metering changes), #4130 (invoice templates)
- Docs PR: docs-site#2857 (release notes draft + FAQ)
- Dashboard: Grafana billing-metrics -> new_sku_rolling_delta (alerts configured)

Launch constraints & acceptance gates (pre-launch):
1) Billing infra tests green: end-to-end invoice generation for 5 seeded accounts mapped to each migration path.
2) Docs & Console copy finalized and staged behind feature flag.
3) Sales enablement deck + FAQ reviewed and ready.
4) Support runbook with rollback and escalation paths published.
5) Legal sign-off on regional contract language (EU/UK).

Rollout windows & phases:
- Phase 0 (canary, 2 business days): internal + partner accounts (up to 25 customers) on NA. Monitor usage delta and invoice parity.
- Phase 1 (staged NA, 2 weeks): 10% of production customers, automatic telemetry gating.
- Phase 2 (full NA, 1 week): all NA customers; EU orgs remain on legacy until legal/compliance sign-off.
- Phase 3 (EU & APAC, 2–3 weeks): regional rollouts once contracts cleared.

Fallback & rollback criteria:
- If invoice mismatch > 1% of expected revenue for two consecutive billing cycles in canary, pause migration and revert instrumentation.
- Any P0 customer-impacting billing error (overbilling or underbilling > $1k) triggers immediate rollback for affected customers and incident review.

Post-launch evaluation:
- 30/90/180-day reports: revenue neutrality check, churn delta for SKUs, average time-to-quote for sales, support ticket volume change related to billing.

Notes on release notes coordination:
- One consolidated release note entry will live in the Billing > Pricing section with granular subsections for Console UI changes, API contract changes (example request/response), migration behavior, and migration timeline.
- SDK changelog to include code snippets for new SKU identifiers and migration examples.

Open questions:
- Do we allow automatic experiments to migrate customers to the simplified pricing for a 30-day A/B test without explicit sign-off? (Proposal: opt-in by account owners; Sales can enroll customers during negotiation.)
- Final SKU naming: internal draft has names Core / Dedicated / Private-Plus. Waiting on brand review (Maya).
